The test image shows soybean plants with mostly green foliage but notable yellowing/chlorosis on some leaves, particularly inner/lower ones. No distinct spots or pustules visible. The pattern suggests possible interveinal chlorosis or systemic disease.

Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome (interveinal chlorosis), Brown_Stem_Rot (similar symptoms), Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus, Downy_mildew.

Now viewing one reference per top candidate:

**Analysis of test image:** Wide canopy view showing soybean plants with scattered yellowing leaves mixed among green foliage. Some leaves are clearly chlorotic/yellowed while upper growth remains green. No discrete spots or pustules visible at this scale. Lower/inner leaves appear more affected.

**Reference comparisons:**
- SDS (field view): Shows patches of yellowing at canopy level - consistent with test image pattern
- Brown Stem Rot: Shows distinct interveinal chlorosis with yellow-green mottling between veins - more pronounced than test
- Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus: Shows discrete yellowish spots on green leaves - doesn't match well
- Downy Mildew: Shows small yellow spots on individual leaves - doesn't match

The scattered yellowing of leaves throughout the canopy while upper growth stays green is most consistent with Sudden_death_syndrome, which causes interveinal chlorosis visible at the canopy level as scattered yellowing/chlorotic leaves while the plant structure remains intact.
